title: Cobalt Systems - POC kickoff & timeline
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood Inference for Cobalt's real-time extraction pipeline. Agreed success criteria (throughput, latency, cost targets, functional pass rate), access plan, benchmark scope, and a timeline with milestones: kickoff, access/setup, mid-point review (week 3), and exec readout (week 6). Action items and next steps enumerated.
next_steps: Send POC SOW and pricing by 2025-12-19
Share security/compliance pack (SOC2 summary, network diagram)
Provision test account and sample dataset + S3 access by 2025-12-22
Schedule mid-point review for week of 2026-01-05
Set up Slack channel and weekly check-ins (Thursdays 10am PT)
action_items: Jordan: Draft and send SOW + pricing (due 2025-12-19)
Priya: Prep benchmark plan and test harness (due 2025-12-21)
Maria: Provide sample dataset and S3 creds (due 2025-12-22)
Alex: Confirm success criteria and exec attendees for readout (due 2025-12-23)
Evan: Confirm network/VPC peering constraints and KMS policy (due 2025-12-24)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros 20
4 i'm Jordan Blake, AE at Redwood.
[00:12] Alex: Hey Jordan, Alex Kim here, head of ML at Cobalt. Maria and Evan are on as well.
[00:18] Maria: hi all, Maria from platform, we manage infra and security.
[00:22] Evan: Evan, CTO.
[00:26] Jordan: Great. The goal today is to scope the POC timeline and milestones 20
4 make sure we agree on success criteria, what we'll benchmark, and who needs access.
[00:36] Priya: Hi all, i'm Priya, solutions engineer. i'll run the bench plan with you and help size the workload.
[00:42] Alex: Great. Quick context 20
4 we have a real-time extraction pipeline, about 250 qps peak across 8k average tokens per request, we're trying to bring down 95th pct latency for inference to under 300ms and keep per-1k token cost below $0.45.
[00:59] Priya: ok that's super helpful. couple clarifying q's: is 250 qps sustained or burst? and how tolerant are you to occasional 500ms spikes?
[01:07] Alex: it's bursty 20
4 sustained around 60-80 qps, spikes to 250 for a few minutes during peak; spike tolerance is minimal for UI flows but batch backfill can be async.
[01:16] Jordan: so for success criteria we often split into functional + performance. From our side a typical POC success matrix: (1) functional correctness 2 outputs match your quality baseline on evaluation prompts; (2) latency SLOs 2 95th <300ms for the interactive path; (3) throughput 2 sustain the target qps with our batching/kv cache enabled; (4) cost 2 meet your unit cost target or show clear path with batching/quantization.
[01:40] Evan: we also need to validate private deployment constraints 2 network peering, KMS, and audit logs. security is non-negotiable.
[01:47] Maria: yep SOC2 and our infosec team will review a network diagram and KMS setup.
[01:52] Priya: noted. We'll include a security checklist in the pack. For the bench: we'll run three scenarios: 1) interactive low-latency (single-turn, 8k tokens avg), 2) bursty sustained scenario to test autoscale to 250 qps, 3) regression tests for quality on your golden prompts.
[02:07] Alex: sounds good. what model family are you recommending?
[02:10] Priya: for this profile we recommend trying an open LLM variant we verified 2 it's lower cost, then fallback to a higher-capacity variant if quality regresses. we'll test both hosted and dedicated profiles; given your security needs we should plan Dedicated or Private trial.
[02:23] Evan: Private would be ideal, but can we start hosted to iterate quickly?
[02:27] Jordan: yes we typically start hosted for bench speed, then move to a dedicated pool or private if the security gating requires it. For timeline i'm proposing 6 weeks: kickoff (this call, week 0), access & setup (week 1), baseline benchmarks + mid-point review (week 3), optimization and final benchmarks (week 5), exec readout (end of week 6).
[02:46] Alex: 6 weeks is OK. can we shorten to 4? we have exec availability the week after next.
[02:51] Priya: compressing is doable if we scope down bench matrix 2 focus only on interactive and golden prompts and skip extended autoscale run; but you'd lose some confidence on burst behavior.
[03:03] Maria: we can't skip network review; that usually takes our sec team a week to sign off.
[03:08] Evan: agree 2 security gating is the long pole.
[03:11] Jordan: ok let's keep 6 weeks nominal, but we'll try to accelerate hosted bench in week 1-2 and aim for mid-point review earlier if security clears.
[03:20] Alex: success criteria 2 to be explicit: 95th pct latency <300ms on interactive path, p95 throughput sustain at 250 qps for 3 minutes during burst test, quality pass rate >= 92% on golden set, cost per 1k tokens <= $0.45 or documented path to it.
[03:36] Priya: i'll put those into the SOW. For sizing 2 you mentioned 8k average tokens; can you share token distribution?
[03:43] Alex: roughly 60% are 2-4k, 30% 4-10k, 10% >10k.
[03:49] Priya: good. that'll influence batching and kv cache hit rates. we'll plan a baseline run with a synthetic replay of that distribution.
[03:56] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[03:58] Jordan: on benchmarks, Priya will run latency microbench, throughput sweep, and quality eval. expected deliverables: bench report with p50/p90/p95, cost estimate per model/quantization profile, and recommendations for Dedicated/private sizing.
[04:13] Priya: for Dedicated pools we usually recommend starting with 4x A100-equivalent capacity or a CPU+GPU mixed config, but we'll produce precise numbers after the baseline.
[04:22] Maria: how long to provision Dedicated or Private environment?
[04:25] Jordan: Hosted can be immediate; Dedicated provisioning typically 3-5 business days once capacity is reserved; Private (VPC peering, KMS) can take 7-14 business days depending on your infra approvals.
[04:37] Evan: and audit logs, retention?
[04:39] Priya: we support audit logging to your S3 and can configure retention and redaction policies; we'll include the sample policy in the security pack.
[04:47] Alex: ok that's helpful. who will own the bench harness on our side?
[04:50] Maria: we'll own data + credentials, but we expect Redwood to run the tests and share the raw logs.
[04:56] Priya: yes we'll run and share raw results and a summarized report.
[05:00] Jordan: timeline and milestones recap I want to lock now: Kickoff (12/18), Access & Setup (by 12/22) 2 Redwood to get S3 + API creds, security pack sent; Baseline bench (12/23-12/29 hosted), Mid-point review (week of 1/5) 2 preliminary findings and tuning, Final optimization & run (1/13-1/16), Exec readout (1/16).
[05:21] Alex: that matches our internal windows except note our exec availability 1/15-1/19, so 1/16 works.
[05:26] Jordan: perfect. any blockers?
[05:28] Maria: need to confirm KMS policy and peering details, i'll open a ticket with infra and aim to have answers by 12/24.
[05:35] Evan: will review SOW and pricing asap.
[05:38] Jordan: action items 2 we'll email the SOW and S3 instructions today, Priya will circulate the benchmark plan.
[05:44] Alex: one more q on fallbacks: if a lower-cost open model fails quality, can Redwood fallback to a larger hosted model mid-POC without starting over?
[05:53] Priya: yes 2 we can swap model variants and keep the same harness, we'll track regressions. there may be cost delta but no major infra change if hosted. Private will require image/version sync but we can coordinate.
[06:05] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[06:07] Jordan: alright let's summarize next steps 2 Jordan send SOW + pricing, Priya send bench plan, Cobalt to provide sample data and creds, infra ticket for KMS/peering, schedule mid-point and exec readout.
[06:19] Alex: that's good. thanks everyone.
[06:21] Maria: thanks.
[06:22] Evan: thanks all.
[06:24] Jordan: we'll follow up with calendar invites and the SOW. end.
